steps.observation: Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
# The Last Light

Old Maren had kept the light for thirty-one years.

She knew the rocks by their sounds — the way Widow's Point hissed when the tide pulled back across it, the hollow knock of the Bell Stone when the swells ran high. She knew the fog the way other people knew old neighbors, recognizing its moods, its tricks, its seasonal temperament.

Every evening at dusk she climbed the iron stairs. Seventy-two steps. She had counted them so many times the number lived in her bones rather than her mind.

On the night of the November storm, the light went out.

The bulb had lasted longer than expected. Still, its failure arrived at the worst possible moment — wind screaming off the Atlantic, a cargo vessel she had watched on the horizon all afternoon now invisible in the dark and the spray. She moved fast, faster than her sixty-three-year-old knees approved of, pulling the spare from its cabinet, working by feel as the room swayed and the windows ran white with water.

When the beam came back, she pressed her forehead against the cold glass and looked out.

The vessel had turned.

She never learned the names of the sailors she saved. She never learned most of their names, across all those years. That was simply the nature of the work — you held the light, and somewhere out in the dark, people found their way home, and they never thought much about why.

Maren thought that was just fine.

She climbed back down the seventy-two steps, put the kettle on, and listened to the storm spend itself against the shore.
